key_insight: Random-subspace intrinsic-dimension analysis shows that materials GNNs can reach similar final accuracy with very different amounts of trainable parameter-space freedom, revealing a new measure of learning difficulty beyond endpoint performance.
engineering_relevance: This gives model developers a stress test for how much optimization capacity CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DimeNet++ need for different property targets, helping guide architecture choice, scaling, and data-efficient design.
method: Train CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DimeNet++ inside randomly oriented parameter subspaces.
Sweep the subspace dimension to measure how performance recovers toward full-model accuracy.
Compare recovery across six property-prediction tasks plus dataset-size and width sweeps.
evidence_signal: Across six tasks, the recovery curves separate final accuracy from trainable-dimensional demand: metallic classification and log-bulk-modulus recover quickly, formation-energy and band-gap are more architecture-dependent, and phonon prediction is most sensitive to dimensional restriction.
watch_item: Random-subspace results reflect a specific training setup and may not translate directly to other optimizers, initialization schemes, or dataset splits.
paper_title: Measuring trainable degrees of freedom in materials graph neural networks: a random-subspace intrinsic dimension analysis
